title: Share derivation rules from entities using minimal structural signatures
context: The scoring rules live in src/lib/features/game/helpers, a frontend Redux module, and the application layer reaches outward to reach them: create-rally and update-rally import from @/lib/features/game/helpers. Deriving statistics needs those same rules on the server. The type-decoupling change deliberately separated domain data shapes from the *View types derived from API response schemas, and restricted components to importing values from entities rather than data shapes, on the stated ground that values do not create coupling but data shapes do.
decision: Move the rules the derivation needs into entities/game.ts as pure functions: deriveSetStats, deriveServingStatus, deriveSetPhase and getPreviousRally, which keeps its get prefix because it is a lookup rather than a computation. Each declares only the minimal structure it actually reads, so both the domain Entry and the presentation EntryView satisfy it structurally and neither caller adopts the other's shape. getSetLineup and getPreviousScores are UI concerns and stay in the frontend. Two conditions make this sound rather than a violation: signatures must not accept Entry[] or Game, and entities must not import server-only modules.

alternatives.option: Leave the rules in lib/features and let the backend keep importing them
alternatives.reason: It cements the inversion and binds the derivation to the Redux view types while the server holds domain types.

alternatives.option: Move all five query helpers at once
alternatives.reason: Their parameters are all *View types, so moving each one is a signature redesign rather than a file move, and getSetLineup resolves which lineup a form should seed, which is UI policy that entities should not absorb.

alternatives.option: Duplicate the rules, one implementation per side
alternatives.reason: Two implementations of the scoring rules drift, and the drift only surfaces when a user sees a wrong score.

consequences: The application layer's outward imports drop from three to one; the remaining one is a request DTO type in the player use case.
Entities gains four functions and no new imports, so it stays free of external dependencies and safe to include in a frontend bundle.
Derivation is invoked in the Redux initialize reducer and stored in state, not called from components, which keeps components on *View types and keeps the computation off the render path.
Query helpers live in two places during the transition, split along domain rule versus UI concern rather than arbitrarily.
revisitTriggers: Entities acquires a server-only dependency, which would turn sharing into a leak and require rethinking the shared boundary.
A moved function's signature is widened to accept a domain data shape, which would reintroduce the coupling type-decoupling removed.
